title: Who Bridges Safety? Identifying and Targeting Cross-Lingual Shared Safety Pathways
abstract: arXiv:2608.09095v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Uncovering the internal mechanisms underlying the safety capabilities of large language models (LLMs) is crucial for developing trustworthy artificial intelligence. Currently, mechanistic interpretability studies on multilingual safety are largely confined to local components, such as isolated neurons. However, this static and fragmented perspective overlooks the synergy among components and fails to elucidate how safety signals dynamically propagate within the model to drive safety decisions ultimately. In this work, we move beyond isolated neurons to identify and target the cross-layer functional pathways formed during safety signal propagation, thereby uncovering the mechanisms driving the cross-lingual safety gap. Specifically, we first identify monolingual safety pathways and validate their impact on refusing harmful requests. translated_title: 谁来架起安全的桥梁？识别并定位跨语言共享安全通路
translated_abstract: 揭示大语言模型（LLM）安全能力背后的内部机制，对于开发可信赖的人工智能至关重要。目前，针对多语言安全的机制可解释性研究大多局限于局部组件，例如孤立的神经元。然而，这种静态且碎片化的视角忽视了组件之间的协同作用，也无法阐明安全信号如何在模型内部动态传播并最终驱动安全决策。在本工作中，我们超越孤立神经元的视角，识别并定位安全信号传播过程中形成的跨层功能通路，从而揭示驱动跨语言安全差距的机制。具体而言，我们首先识别单语安全通路，并验证了其对拒绝有害请求的影响。随后的跨语言分析揭示了一组稀疏的跨语言共享安全通路……
tldr: 该研究超越孤立神经元的静态分析，识别并定位大语言模型中安全信号传播的跨层功能通路，发现稀疏的跨语言共享安全通路是造成跨语言安全差距的关键机制，为提升模型多语言安全能力提供了新思路。
en_tdlr: This work moves beyond isolated neurons to identify and target cross-layer safety signal propagation pathways in LLMs, revealing that a sparse set of cross-lingual shared safety pathways underlies the cross-lingual safety gap, offering a new approach for improving multilingual safety.
